utterances.text: We certainly don't have the map, and I would be assisted if the Prosecution were able to help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We will report, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then we will have a break, and we will resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, just to come back to one point, did you have a chance over the break to have look at your statements?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And am I right when I say that the first time that "military governor" is used is at page 50 of your third statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And it was suggested to you by Thomas Elfgren, a member of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during Thomas Elfgren's interview, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And am I also right that no basis was provided by him to you as to his conclusion that you agreed with?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can just take you back now to the subject of Mr. Cermak's authority, as you have alleged? Just let me establish this, Mr. Berikoff: Would it be fair to say and accurate that you neither heard nor saw Mr. Cermak order any troops on the ground, whether they be police or army? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your assumption is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: You had, however, seen Major Juric, you heard and seen him give orders on the ground, had you not?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: On numerous occasions, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm not going to deal with freedom of movement in any great detail with you, given what you have told me in the last session. But can I just establish this: Were you aware, as information officer, that freedom of movement was, in fact, negotiated in Zagreb and was available in the form of the Akashi agreement? Is that something that you knew about?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And the letter that was issued to you by Mr. Cermak was, in fact, a facilitating letter, a transmission of what had been agreed at a higher level. Would you understand that to be fair?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd understand that to be correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And, in fact, just to put it in its full context, it is right to say that you had described Mr. Cermak's letter as a joke?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Because whenever it was presented at any of the check-points or any time we tried to use that letter for freedom of movement, it was virtually disregarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And it's also right that, in fact, General Forand asked you not to use the letter as much as possible, but just try to push the envelope. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. That is a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'd like to now turn to a new topic, which is the denial, according to you, of crimes by Mr. Cermak and your allegation that could you have stopped them. And to be fair to you again, Mr. Berikoff, I'm going to check with you whether or not you have been privy to certain documentation which provides a context to my questions. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, from your statements, we know that you have said that Mr. Cermak was told about burning and looting and that it must stop by General Forand. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And just so that you know, we are informed in this courtroom of correspondence that took place between the two gentlemen, all right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, in your third statement at page 31, if you need to lock at it, on a couple of occasions, you say, you were present when General Cermak and General Forand had their discussions.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Can you help me with when?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the dates, ma'am. I know there were a couple of times when I was in the room when they had discussed the issue. There were other occasions when I stood outside with the General's personal body-guard, and was not privy to the information that went on in the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Trouble is, we can't find your name and we have a lot of reports. And if could you give me a date, we could and find you. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot provide a date, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: You say, in your third statement, that during this conversation you say you were privy to, you didn't pay any attention to it. Why was that, if you were information officer?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at a much higher level than I was interested in. I was interested in the situation on the ground itself, and that was between the senior management. So, therefore, my interests were elsewhere, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I know that's a long time ago now, over 13 years. Could it, in fact, be the case that what you're referring to in terms of being present at a conversation is, in fact, having been told about what was said?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, ma'am. I was in the office on a couple of occasions with General Cermak and a number of other people and General Forand. Most of the time, as I indicated, I was outside in the hall or other places with his personal body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Let go to the specific, if we may, of what you say about the crime denials. If you will take it from me, I will try and put into a nutshell what it is is that you've said; and, of course, Mr. Berikoff, if you wish to check it, you may do so and I can give you the reference.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine, ma'am. I will take your word.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: The first statement that you give, you refer to: "Cermak denied knowledge of any of his troops conducting the looting and arson. I would disagree with the argument that those who were responsible for the criminal acts were criminals out of control. There might have been someone who to the opportunity to take revenge, but they would have been very, very few. Now, in that statement, and, again, I'm referring to the document, can you confirm for me, Mr. Berikoff, that you don't identify who you mean by "troops"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Correct. Now, to put it in context, and to be fair to you, I want to give you an opportunity to look at what was recorded about that revenge comment at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And I'd like, please, to have on the screen D56.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just to put it into context, while that is being uploaded, this is a report of the 18th of August, 1995, written by Mr. Al-Alfi. You know ho was, do you?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the name, ma'am. If you give me his position, I may recall who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: He was referred to see at the PHAC?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that acronym, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: He was involved in writing of the reports. This reports goes from him to UNCRO HQ Zagreb which you can see on the screen, and he was present at many meetings at which General Forand was present.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If could I ask, please, for the third page of this document to be put before the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when I say the PHAC, the UN head of civil affairs, all right? If you can just have a look now at the second paragraph there, because what he is referring to here is a meeting with General Cermak. Other participants, in fact, in this meeting were Flynn, Tymchuk, and Roberts, all of whom you know. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Sir?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, ma'am. I'm sorry. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If we can just now look at the second paragraph which begins: "During the meeting," you'll see that it states: "I also brought the attention of General Cermak our concern about the continuing reports of houses and farms set on fire." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] "... and looting, and asked him about the measures taken from his side to stop such acts. General Cermak shared this concern with us and expressed his unhappiness about its continuation. He promised tough action against those who commit such acts. He also explained that some of these acts may be carried out by civilians who returned to the area and seek revenge, taking advantage of the lifting of restrictions on their movement in the area." Now, sharing with you the context of those remarks, would you agree with me that it was, in fact, not a denial, but that document from the time reflects that General Cermak shared concerns, expressed his unhappiness, and he does promise action? Do you see that? Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that in the report, yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like, please, to upload D151 to deal with further alleged denials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, in the previous document, we see some comment on the first page, and it might not have caught my attention earlier, like Cermak versus Mayor of Knin. I don't know whether that is a Court case. I don't know where it comes from. But it might that be it has been explained to us at an earlier stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Your Honour, it is not in evidence. It is certainly not a note that has been made on the document from the Defence. It was actually on the document when we received it from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then, it remains a mystery for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: This is a report, again, from Mr. Al-Alfi up to UNCRO HQ Zagreb, dated 24th of August, 1995. And this is it a report concerning a meeting between General Forand and General Cermak, and you'll see there what General Forand has referred to General Cermak as. What I'm concerned is the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If that can be uploaded, please, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Looking again at the context of the meeting, it refers to the following, if can you read it through. It concerns the bringing of attention to the burning houses and looting in the area to General Cermak, asking him to stop such acts. The record reads that he accepted this fact regarding the continuation of such incidents and attributed them to person who entered the area wearing HV uniforms and to civilians taking revenge. He also attributed such facts to ongoing acts -- rather, to ongoing efforts by the Croatian army who are still clearing the terrain and capturing the rebels. "General Cermak made it clear that in his opinion, the area is very vast and he would be lying if he told us nothing of the sort would continue to happen but he informed us that he has already issued strict orders to the civilian and military personnel to stop such acts." Now, would you agree with me, Mr. Berikoff, having looked at this contemporaneous document from the time, that importantly, again, in this context Mr. Cermak was admitting that crimes were taking place?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree in that context, ma'am, and there were times when I learned from General Forand that, in fact, General Cermak had said that this was going on. He was not able to stop all of it, and that it was possibly as reported in that report. Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: D59, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, I think it is right to say that would you have come across certain press articles, but you clarified to me that were spending most of your time out on the terrain. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: D59, as it is coming up on to the screen, I'd like to ask you whether you got to see this article in any form. And it's an article dated the 7th of September, 1995, entitled: "Cermak, there is no place for looters in the HV, Croatian army." Did you see that at that time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have. I don't recall the article itself, but I may have or I may have heard about it, yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Looking at the context of that first paragraph, because that is really what I'm interested in, according to Colonel-General Ivan Cermak, commander of the Knin assembly point: "A large-scale operation has been launched to resolve problems relating to the illegal appropriation of apartments and the looting and torching homes, acts regrettably most often committed by members of the Croatian army. Some ten warrants have already been issued for arresting and bringing before the military court in Split such soldiers who, as General Cermak stated, defile the Croatian army and have no place in it." You would agree with me, Mr. Berikoff, not a denial of crime, is it?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to agree with you, according to that article, yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yeah. As well as press articles, were you also sometimes privy to reports in the media concerning television or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, ma'am. I did not watch television while I was there. We didn't have access to it once the offensive started.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is to show you a clip because it goes to this issue that you're raising.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: This is a clip that has been served, in fact, Your Honour, by the Prosecution. It's the subject of recent disclosure. It's 2D05-0001. And before it is played, if I can just assist in terms of its provenance, we understand from its context that it would have been perhaps a month after Operation Storm, we estimate in the first week of September, and it's a HRAT video news broadcast served by the Prosecution last month. Your Honours, transcripts - or rather, translations have been provided to the both. It is a very short clip, if I could ask for it to be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The video-clip can be played.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I pose the question, can I say that there was no transcript coming across in my earpiece; however, what I would ask that this clip be exhibited along with the transcript of the video, so that it can be readily recognised to what was stated, if that is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must admit I was reading rather the translation, rather than listening to it. One of the problems is that we -- I don't know whether there was French translation provided. I'm asking the French booth. I have difficulties in seeing who is exactly behind what smoke window, but was there any spoken French so we have a complete translation?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes. There was French interpretation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the English, therefore, has not been transcribed. Now, we can resolve this in various ways. If you would tender the English transcript and if we have the French translation on the French audio, that would mean that it will be transcribed soon, because as far as I understand - but correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Registrar - the French transcripts are made on the basis of the audio recordings that are sent to a specialised agency, that we would then have a full record, and by the explanation I now give, it is explained on the record as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we now have, for the completeness of the record, we have the B/C/S and English transcripts together with the video. On the video, by the way, the -- no, the English did not spoken. We have that B/C/S and English transcript then tendered being part of the record; we have for the French, we'll have the French transcript of the words spoken by the French interpreters, which gives a complete record. So we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. Could I ask for the video to be exhibited, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I take it that it was obtained recently by an RFA, if I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Then the video accompanied by the English transcript and the B/C/S transcript, Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D731, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D731 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: To put this into context, Mr. Berikoff, you have seen now a number of clips and, again, contemporaneous materials from the time, and you have heard what General Cermak has had to say about crimes that were brought to his attention. On the back of that, it's right to say, isn't it, that you yourself, within the course of the statements on four occasions - and I'll bring them to your attention - it's right that you had doubts even then about his ability to stop the crimes.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to agree with you, because as I travelled throughout the sector, even after these clips that you have shown me and the various reports, throughout all of my travels, and I travelled extensively throughout the sector, looting was still ongoing and it did not stop. It was still being conducted by the HV, the special police, and paramilitary organisations such as warlords.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Those doubts that you have expressed, as I've stated, are to you found, in fact, in your first statement, your third statement on two occasions, and the last statement where you say: "I believe that General Cermak either did not have the authority to stop the burning and looting or didn't want to stop it"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am. I believe, at that time, his authority -- people just disregarded it in many instances, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Leading on from the disregard of authority, what I'd like to do now is to just give some chance to take a look at the diagram that you prepared, if you recall, and that's P745.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If that could be brought up on to the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, just as a little bit of background to this diagram, would it be fair to say that you didn't receive any specific training, Mr. Berikoff, on the Croatian army or the police structure during your time in the area?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time in the area, no, I did not ma'am. Basically, we didn't have any, and it was one of my taskings to go out and see what units were in the area prior to the offensive, and, again, after to see what activity was going on and who conducting what activity, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And to summarize what you told me before, your focus was on the territory not the individuals. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is it correct. The personality issue was going to come on later had I stayed on in Sector South, but I moved on to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, you prepared the diagram at the time of your first interview in 1996?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And there's a name on your statement. Can you tell me who Cameron Troy Hillier who was present during that statement? Do you remember who he was?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Canadian Military Police police corporal, I believe, ma'am, that was just in attendance as a witness to the interview because I was in the military at the time and the military police were required to be there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, the diagram, was that made at the conclusion of the interview?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. It was done right at the time that I was asked if I could provide a diagram, not after the interview, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: So it was while the interview was going on?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And who had input into the diagram, please?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just I did, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain to me an immediate difficulty with this diagram. Perhaps can you help me. At the time that you made this diagram, it was at the time of the first statement; whereas, you recall you describe Mr. Cermak as a mayor which, as we know, is a civilian position, and I think you would agree with me that that is very different from what we see on your diagram, which refers to, and to be fair to you, probably the military leadership in Sector South. Now, just to be clear, Mr. Berikoff, all I want at the moment is the reason why this difference appears, not the basis for what you have put down on that document there. Can you help with that in any way?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. Because he was known as General Cermak, you could have called him anything you wanted at the time. He was still the senior military person in the area, as far as I was aware of. Therefore, I put him as the person in charge of the military, whether he was called mayor, governor, pope, or anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: You understand that mayor, governor, pope, or anything is not military is it, Mr. Berikoff?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am, but he was also a general, so he was is military.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, that is an assumption you made it terms of -- it may have been a title.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only his title. When he came to the compound, he was in a military uniform, so I saw him as a soldier, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I understand that, and I don't take any disputes with you there, Mr. Berikoff, in fact --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: -- in terms of the uniform and the title. Don't misunderstand me, okay? We agree on that.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: My difficulty was on the difference between the reference in the statement and what you've put down here. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. But my difficulty is that he was in uniform, wearing the rank of general; therefore, I assumed that he was in charge of the military, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And at that time, to be fair again, you had very limited information available to you, in terms of any document resources. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, before I just take you a little bit more into the detail of this document, I'd like to ask you whether or not, during the course of your contact with the Prosecution, you've ever been given the chance to retract this document on the basis of its inaccuracy or contradiction to the Prosecution's own case?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, ma'am. Because once I started employment at the Tribunal, my contact with the investigation team that were working on the Cermak, Gotovina, Markac trial was extremely limited. There were only two occasions when I had conduct with the team regarding the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I understand that. And I think you would agree with me that this a rough diagram rather than a considered piece?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, a draft, draft copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Something one might write on the back of a cigarette box, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're correct in that assumption.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now you said yesterday that the basis for the hierarchy was information that you had gathered and information that you had received from UNCRO. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Tell me if you're not, Mr. Berikoff, but are you in a position to give me the name of any two-legged human sources for what you've written down here, the names?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now Captain Williams who was at the Canadian -- he was a Canadian G2 in Zagreb. He would have provided some information while I was in country, trying to ascertain the order of battle. Naturally, Colonel Tymchuk, General Forand, General Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just stop there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm concerned about your word "would have," as can you understand. We're concerned here, Mr. Berikoff, with, as I know you know, hard fact, all right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I don't want "would have." I'd like to know the names precisely of those people who provided this information to you. If you can't give it to me, just say so?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give it to you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to confirm one point which I think I may have raised earlier, please confirm for me that there are no documentary sources at all, be it orders or anything else, that forms the basis of what you have written on this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's not, ma'am. That is it strictly my own assumption from that period in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And, finally, on this aspect, could you please name me any Croatian human source that you had spoken to that directly contributed to the creation of this document, if any. If you can't, just say so.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ivan Juric and Ivan Cermak, let's deal with that briefly, if we may. If we look at the Ivan Juric box, you have put down here, "special police," and I think you have told us, however, in your various statements that he said to you he was head of the military police. Do you agree that what's down on this document is inconsistent with what you've previously said?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not inconsistent; it's, yes, I have the words "special police," but I also saw Major Juric on numerous occasions in grey coverall uniforms, which I assumed were part of the special police, and every time we spoke to him, he was dealing with both the military police and the special police, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: So to use your words, it was what you'd assumed?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. Who appointed Major Juric; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: As information officer, did you take any time or energy, or were you unable to do so to find out who he was?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unable to do so. I was tasked otherwise. If anybody had, it would have been Captain Hill that had any closer contact with Major Juric.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Geoff Hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm moving on to my next question. Again, just to be sure, you've put a line down there between General Cermak and Major Juric. But so that I'm sure, it's right to say that there isn't a single document or anything that you have seen to support that line. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you help me with this. You have subordinated to Juric, according to the lines that you have drawn and what you said yesterday, the local Croatian police and the special police. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Can you help me with this. Who was the commander of the police station in Knin; do you know?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Okay. And what about the chief of Knin-Kotar police administration?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can help me with the chief of the Zadar-Knin police administration.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's try the deputy minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: One more, the minister of interior at the time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: All right. I'll stop there. Now, I'd like you to look at a Prosecution organigram, which is P500 for the screen, please, just to give you a chance to see what the Prosecution have entered into this case, in terms of what we're talking about here which is hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could, Your Honour, I'm not sure what the relevance is of educating the witness as to what the Prosecution's theory of the hierarchy is. He has clearly indicated what his assumption of it was. The basis for that has been explored. I don't see how it will assist the Chamber to show the witness what the Prosecution thinks about that particular portion of the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm not asking him that, Your Honour. That is not my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then ... I think, as a matter of fact, what Ms. Higgins did is to give a context or a framework in which she would put questions to the witness. Whether it was very wise to say to give a chance to the witness to say, You can comment on what the Prosecution puts, let's listen to the questions, Mr. Russo, and then see whether there are any further objections. But before doing so, I'd like to, first of all, ask your attention for the pauses, which message appears on our screen, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second, to the clock. I said we would finish today by 1.30. So before starting perhaps a new series of questions, perhaps we should conclude for the day and give the usual instructions to the witness. Mr. Berikoff --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will finish for the day. I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, the -- witness the 3rd of September, 9.00, in this same courtroom. And we adjourn until then and resume tomorrow, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd of September, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
